The manifest tells browsers which asset names to request. We upload every new asset under its versioned name before switching the manifest so that any browser fetching the new manifest can load everything it references.

We keep the old assets because a browser that already fetched the previous manifest may still request those names after the switch. Keeping them available lets those requests succeed.

**f1** Upload all new assets under versioned names before switching the manifest. A browser can fetch the new manifest as soon as it’s published, so every file it references must already be available. Switching earlier could send browsers to files that haven’t finished uploading.

**f2** Keep the old assets available because a browser that fetched the previous manifest still uses the filenames listed there. It may request a file after the switch, for example when someone opens a feature for the first time. Keeping that file at its original URL lets the feature load.
